# Report — focus-follow across monitors

**Status: implemented, CI green, drop shipped.** Plan:
[20260820-100824_focus-follow-monitor.plan.qmd](20260820-100824_focus-follow-monitor.plan.qmd).
Commit `89f2294` on `master` (jiangyun-fun/hunt-and-peck).

## What was done

1. `OverlayViewModel.SwitchToMonitor(Rect)` (`src/HuntAndPeck/ViewModels/OverlayViewModel.cs`):
   finds the session whose `OwningWindowBounds` equals the given monitor bounds and
   `LoadSession`s it — the same swap `CycleMonitor` makes (Bounds change → the view
   repositions; labels regenerate; prefix + pan reset). No-op on no match, on
   same-monitor, and whenever `CanFollowForegroundMonitor` is false (single-session,
   zone, quadrant modes).
2. `OverlayView` foreground-monitor poll (`src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs`):
   a 200 ms `DispatcherTimer`, started on load only when the VM is follow-capable,
   stopped on close. Edge-triggered: it acts only when the foreground window's monitor
   differs from the last seen one, so Tab cycling (which does not move focus) is never
   fought. Monitor identity = `Screen.FromHandle(GetForegroundWindow()).Bounds`
   (physical px, same WinForms API the sessions were built from).
3. Tests (`src/HuntAndPeck.Tests/ViewModels/OverlayViewModelTest.cs`): 3 new facts —
   landscape↔portrait swap with prefix/pan reset; same/unknown-monitor no-op (prefix
   survives); capability gates for single-session and quadrant mode.
4. `CLAUDE.md`: new "Focus-follow across monitors" bullet.

## Notes / caveats

- Portrait correctness is inherited: each monitor's session is pre-built for its own
  bounds (per-aspect zone alignment), so the switch is a geometry-correct swap with
  no re-enumeration.
- Cross-DPI moves use the load-time cached transform — identical to existing Tab
  cycling (process is system-DPI aware; no per-monitor manifest in the repo).
- Quadrant / zone / Automation overlays intentionally do not follow (documented in
  CLAUDE.md); a follow-with-rebuild for quadrant mode would be a separate change.
